The main takeaway from our work is that

marine cyanobacteria have evolved an unprecedented mechanism of lanthipeptide biosynthesis and that this mechanism is the driving force of an evolutionary radiation process that favors the emergence of novel lanthipeptide structures over the refinement of an existing structure.

prochlorosins are an excellent example of how natural product diversification can arise from an evolutionary process favoring the sustained creation of new structures over the refinement of an existing structure.
the evolutionary radiation of prochlorosis has led to an extensive diversification of their peptide structures, which is not constrained by the biosynthetic machinery.
